result.title: Interpreting Timestamp Permutations in Dynamic Link Prediction
result.comment: 5 pages total (ACM sigconf format). Companion code and trained models: https://github.com/karpovilia/tgn
result.summary: Timestamp permutations are used to test whether dynamic link predictors exploit temporal information, but a performance gap can reflect changes in training, evaluation history, or both. We separate these effects with a crossed diagnostic and measure input exposure: whether altered histories actually change the predictor's inputs. On MOOC, TCL trained with binary cross-entropy gains approximately eight pairwise-accuracy points from original-chronology training under either evaluation history, while changing history at fixed weights gives only 0.03 points. The small history contrast reflects unchanged inputs for 68.37% of queries, stable rankings for most others, and cancellation of gains and losses. Under original evaluation history, suppressing explicit time encoding reduces the training contrast from 8.03 to 3.64 points, a paired reduction of 4.39 points (95% interval [3.68, 5.09]) across six seeds. DyGFormer shows corresponding training and history contrasts of 22.34 and 0.38 points across two seeds, despite greater exposure. Partial history permutations further separate nominal intervention strength, input changes, and aggregate accuracy. These comparisons turn a single permutation gap into interpretable statements about training conditions and model responses, while leaving the internal mechanisms of temporal learning open.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在动态链接预测中拆解时间戳置换带来的性能差距，用交叉诊断与「输入暴露」度量区分训练时序与评测历史两种来源，并显示时序编码被抑制后训练对比显著缩小。
AI.relevance_reason: 其交叉诊断与输入暴露度量可供核查如何区分「评测期证据真正改变了输入与内部状态」与「仅在训练期形成的偏置」，对 LOOK/THINK 的因果贡献分配与干预强度解释有方法借鉴。
